skill.name: infsh-cli
skill.description: Guide Claude, Codex, and Claude Code through the inference.sh CLI to discover and run hosted AI apps for media, language, search, and automation.
skill.summary: Discover, configure, run, and monitor hosted inference.sh apps from the belt CLI.
skill.author: inferen-sh

security_audit.summary: The documentation contains repeated remote installer commands that pipe live content to a shell, plus an unsafe manifest-driven download command. It also enables local file uploads and public social media actions without explicit consent controls; most other alerts are Markdown or documentation false positives.

remediation.issue: Remote installer content is piped directly to sh.
remediation.suggestion: Replace every pipe-to-shell command with a version-pinned download, then verify a separately anchored checksum and Sigstore signature before execution.

remediation.issue: The manual download parses a remote manifest with grep and unquoted command substitution.
remediation.suggestion: Use a structured JSON parser, validate the selected HTTPS URL, quote every expansion, pin a release version, and verify before installation.

remediation.issue: Local paths are uploaded without an explicit consent or sensitivity step.
remediation.suggestion: Require confirmation before each upload, display the resolved path and destination, and restrict uploads to user-approved directories.

remediation.issue: Social media commands can publish content without a required confirmation.
remediation.suggestion: Generate a preview and require explicit user approval immediately before any post, direct message, follow, like, or repost action.

remediation.issue: The related belt CLI skill installation is unpinned.
remediation.suggestion: Make the dependency optional, pin it to an immutable audited revision, and explain that it expands the security review boundary.

content.user_title: Run AI Apps with the inference.sh CLI
content.value_statement: Using many hosted AI models from a terminal requires different app names, inputs, and task flows. This skill provides focused inference.sh CLI guidance.
actual_capabilities: Search and filter the public inference.sh app catalog.
Inspect app details and generate sample input files.
Run image, video, language, search, audio, and 3D apps.
Upload user-selected local media as app inputs.
Submit long-running tasks and retrieve their status or results.
Guide local testing and deployment of inference.sh apps.
limitations: Requires the external belt CLI, an inference.sh account, network access, and available credits.
App names, model availability, schemas, prices, and outputs can change outside this skill.
Local files may be uploaded to a hosted service when their paths are used as inputs.
Installation and social media actions require careful user review because they have external effects.

use_cases.title: Create Media Prototypes
use_cases.description: Find and run image or video apps, then monitor long-running generation tasks.

use_cases.title: Evaluate Hosted Models
use_cases.description: Compare language, search, speech, and media apps through repeatable CLI inputs.

use_cases.title: Automate App Operations
use_cases.description: Inspect, test, deploy, and invoke inference.sh apps from development or CI workflows.

prompt_templates.title: Find an App
prompt_templates.prompt: Find inference.sh apps for [task]. Show the most relevant choices and explain their main differences before running anything.

prompt_templates.title: Prepare a Safe Run
prompt_templates.prompt: Inspect [app-name], create a sample input for [goal], and show the planned command. Ask before submitting the task.

prompt_templates.title: Run and Track a Task
prompt_templates.prompt: Run [app-name] with [input-file] after confirming any local uploads. Return the task identifier, status, and final output location.

prompt_templates.title: Build a Reproducible Workflow
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a version-pinned inference.sh workflow for [project]. Validate schemas, protect secrets, confirm uploads, monitor tasks, and document failure recovery.

output_examples.input: Find a fast app for generating a short landscape video.
output_examples.output: Recommended app: Google Veo Fast. The response summarizes expected inputs, notes account costs, and asks before task submission.

output_examples.input: Track my submitted image generation task.
output: The hosted download location is ready for review.

output_examples.input: Prepare an image upscaling run for a local photo.
output_examples.output: The response identifies the resolved local path, explains that it will be uploaded, and requests approval before running the app.

best_practices: Inspect each app schema and generate a sample input before the first run.
Pin app versions and preserve task identifiers for reproducible workflows.
Confirm costs, local file uploads, credentials, and external account changes before execution.
anti_patterns: Do not pipe remote installer output directly into a shell.
Do not place API keys in prompts, command history, source files, or saved examples.
Do not publish social content or upload local files without explicit user approval.

faq.question: What must be installed?
faq.answer: The external belt CLI is required. Review and verify its installer before installation.

faq.question: Does this skill run models locally?
faq.answer: No. It submits work to hosted inference.sh apps, so network access and an account are required.

faq.question: How are credentials provided?
faq.answer: Use belt login for interactive authentication or the INFSH_API_KEY environment variable for controlled automation.

faq.question: Can it use local files?
faq.answer: Yes. Paths supplied as compatible inputs are uploaded, so confirm the exact file and destination first.

faq.question: How are long tasks monitored?
faq.answer: Submit with the no-wait option, preserve the task identifier, and query the task until completion.

faq.question: Can it post to Twitter or X?
faq.answer: The catalog includes account automation apps. Require a preview and explicit approval before any public or private action.
